newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy probes whether train crash caused by speed.
newsitem.headline: Italy probes whether train crash caused by speed.

text.p: Italian authorities on Monday focused on speed as a possible cause for the derailment of an express train in northern Italy that killed eight people.

The Milan-to-Rome high-speed "Pendolino" train shot off the tracks as it rounded a curve a short distance before the Piacenza station on Sunday afternoon. The train's two engineers were among the victims and another 30 passengers were injured.

Police, firefighters and railroad employees continued to clear debris from the tracks on Monday as Piacenza's public prosecutor's office, Italy's Ferrovie dello Stato railway and the Transport Ministry opened investigations into the cause.
Investigators said the train's "black box" or recorder, which was recovered on Sunday, would be studied to determine how fast it had been travelling when it left the track.
Rail officials have said regulations required trains not to exceed 105 km per hour (60 mph) around the Piacenza curve.
Italian media reported on Monday, citing unnamed sources, that the black box showed the train had been travelling at 163 km per hour (102 mph).
Piacenza's public prosecutor, Alberto Grassi, refused to comment on the reports, saying any information about the train's speed would be released at the end of his inquiry.
Delays of up to three hours in rail services between northern and southern Italy were reported as trains continued to be diverted around Piacenza.
The COMU union representing Italy's train drivers issued a statement late on Sunday in which it said human error was not to blame and blasted the railway for "lax safety checks".
The union said it would stage a strike from noon to 2 p.m. (1100-1300 GMT) on Thursday to draw attention to its claims of safety problems.
The railway's managing director Giancarlo Cimolo said Italy's trains were "the safest in Europe".
